answer: Cross-Epoch Behavioural Consistency Rule. Each identity carries a cedar-scored history vector of task types, timing, and counterparties. At epoch boundaries, agents must submit a plume of recent action hashes; a consistency check compares them against the prior trajectory via a rotating prism of similarity thresholds. Identities whose behaviour diverges beyond tolerance are quarantined until reconciled. Sybils pay by having to sustain plausible, correlated histories across many epochs, multiplying maintenance cost per fake identity.
